note: sample = id of a recorded instrument in sound-engine/library/samples/index.json (played when loaded); the other fields are the hand-synthesized fallback, 'inspired by' each instrument. harmonics = amplitudes of partials 1,2,3... (they follow the envelope); partials = extra {ratio, amp, decay} tones, each with its own decay (bright string attacks, bar/plate modes, detuned beating); envelope = ADSR seconds (sustain 0..1); noise = breath/pick/buzz burst; brightness 0..1 (lower = darker); dur = note length in seconds; octave = shift. Optional: vibrato {rate Hz, depth cents, delay s}; slide {cents, time}: start that many cents away and glide in; wah {rate Hz, harmonics}: alternate to these harmonics and back (formant sweep); gesture = a short idiomatic phrase for timbre-atlas: scale cents (+ period), steps (scale degrees), gap s between notes, dur, hold (notes overlap), tremolo {count, gap} on the last note (tremoloAll: every note), bend {cents, at, time} on the last note, slideEach (every note slides in). Drum patterns: gesture.rhythm (onsets in gaps), accents (amp per step), fixedHz (drum's own pitch).
